svg.title: Agent track: a MAF agent keeps the task board up to date
svg.desc: At the second stand-up, the agent calls get_board, which loads three open cards into its context. It reads the transcript in order. Fire alarm test is on the board, so it calls update_card with done. The readings are on the board, so update_card with progress and the note Made a start. The contractor booking is on the board, so update_card with blocked and the note Waiting on supplier. Ordering parts for the Atlas is not on the board, so it calls find_equipment, which returns Air Compressor 1, then create_card. A remark about testing the long belt has no card and is not a new job, so it makes no call. The board then becomes the starting point for the next stand-up.

g.text: Agent track: the board is the agent's memory
A MAF agent reads the stand-up, checks the board through tools, and decides for itself: update what exists, create what doesn't.
Stand-up 2 · the agent starts from yesterday's board (3 open cards)
the agent reads it in order
Grace: Tested the long belt, fine.
GPT-5.6 Luna · reads the transcript itself
Board: #1 GT1 readings · #2 Fire alarm test · #3 Book contractor
“Fire alarm test's done” → on the board? yes, #2 → done
“order Atlas parts” → on the board? no → new card
“Tested the long belt” → no card, not a new job → skip
Finished: 4 changes from 6 tool calls, each with a quote
Next stand-up: get_board() returns this board, so the agent starts from what it built
Design only. It reuses the board track's data, scoring and UI, and GPT-5.6 Luna like the pipeline. It will be compared on updates right, wrong closes, duplicates, cost and run-to-run spread.
